nodes.summary: Thompson's group $F$ is the group with generators $x_0, x_1$ and relations $[x_0 x_1^{-1}, x_0^{-1} x_1 x_0] = 1$ and $[x_0 x_1^{-1}, x_0^{-2} x_1 x_0^2] = 1$, where $[a, b] = a b a^{-1} b^{-1}$; that is, the quotient of the free group on $x_0, x_1$ by the normal subgroup generated by these two relators.
nodes.title: Thompson's group $F$ by its standard presentation

nodes.summary: It is not the case that the intersection of any two finitely generated subgroups of Thompson's group $F$ is finitely generated: there are finitely generated subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $F$ such that $H \cap K$ is not finitely generated.
nodes.title: Thompson's group $F$ does not have the Howson property

nodes.summary: The statement that Thompson's group $F$ has the Howson property: for all finitely generated subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $F$, the intersection $H \cap K$ is finitely generated.
nodes.title: Howson property for Thompson's group $F$

nodes.summary: In the free group on two generators $x_0$ and $x_1$, this is the set of the two elements $[x_0 x_1^{-1}, x_0^{-1} x_1 x_0]$ and $[x_0 x_1^{-1}, x_0^{-2} x_1 x_0^2]$, where $[a, b] = a b a^{-1} b^{-1}$. They are the relators of the standard presentation of Thompson's group $F$.
nodes.title: Relators of Thompson's group $F$

conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
